record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: How do nuclear antishadowing or EMC effects in spin-dependent structure functions g1 and g2 modify the polarized Bjorken sum rule, and what does that imply for axial-current nuclear radiative corrections in mirror or other nuclear beta decays?

evidence.quote: For the axial current, its effect depends on the (anti)shadowing of the spin-dependent structure functions, g1,2 (148).

While these have received less attention than their spin-independent partners, initial studies (149, 150) have shown a stronger EMC effect for spin-polarized structure functions (151, 152, 153, 154). The effects on the polarized Bjorken sum rule have not been explicitly researched, however, and require further study.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let g_1^N(x,Q^2) and g_2^N(x,Q^2) denote the spin-dependent inclusive deep-inelastic structure functions of a nucleon N (proton p or neutron n) at Bjorken variable x ∈ (0,1) and momentum transfer Q^2. The polarized Bjorken sum rule states that

  Γ_1^{p−n}(Q^2) := ∫_0^1 [ g_1^p(x,Q^2) − g_1^n(x,Q^2) ] dx = (g_A/6) · C_{Bj}(Q^2),

where g_A is the nucleon isovector axial coupling and C_{Bj}(Q^2) is the perturbative QCD Wilson coefficient.

For a nucleus A regarded as an isospin doublet partner of its mirror A' (e.g. ^3He–^3H), define the in-medium spin-dependent structure functions g_1^{A,A'}(x,Q^2), g_2^{A,A'}(x,Q^2) and the nuclear analogue

  Γ_1^{A−A'}(Q^2) := ∫_0^1 [ g_1^A(x,Q^2) − g_1^{A'}(x,Q^2) ] dx.

Nuclear modifications of these structure functions, relative to the naive sum over free nucleons, are conventionally separated into shadowing (small x), antishadowing (x ≈ 0.1), the EMC region (0.3 ≲ x ≲ 0.7), and Fermi motion (x → 1). Recent model studies indicate that the spin-dependent EMC effect is stronger than its spin-independent counterpart.

Problem. 
(a) Quantify how nuclear (anti)shadowing and the spin-dependent EMC effect in g_1 and g_2 modify the polarized Bjorken sum rule when applied to a nuclear isospin doublet (A, A'); i.e. compute the deviation

  Δ_A(Q^2) := Γ_1^{A−A'}(Q^2) − (g_A^{A−A'}/6) · C_{Bj}(Q^2),

where g_A^{A−A'} is the nuclear axial-vector matrix element for the A → A' Gamow–Teller transition, and exhibit Δ_A as an explicit functional of the in-medium modifications of g_{1,2}.

(b) Translate the result of (a) into a correction to the axial-current contribution to the inner radiative correction for nuclear (in particular mirror) β decays of the doublet (A, A'), and determine its size relative to the corresponding free-nucleon axial radiative correction.

Provide either an analytic dispersive expression or a quantitative estimate, and identify the kinematic region (shadowing, antishadowing, or EMC) that dominates the effect.
artifact.category_tag: Polarized Bjorken sum rule and nuclear beta decay
artifact.status_search_result: The polarized (spin) EMC effect on g_1 and the in-medium Bjorken sum rule has been studied in mean-field nuclear models (e.g. arXiv:2006.10601, "Gamow-Teller transitions and the spin EMC effect: the Bjorken sum-rule in medium"), and an EMC-type effect in spin structure functions is the target of JLab proposal PR12-14-001. However, no dedicated calculation of the implied modification of the axial-current nuclear radiative correction for mirror β decays appears in the literature; the question of how (anti)shadowing and EMC effects in g_{1,2} feed into the polarized Bjorken sum rule and into nuclear axial radiative corrections is explicitly flagged as requiring further study and remains open.

status_evidence.title: Gamow-Teller transitions and the spin EMC effect: the Bjorken sum-rule in medium
status_evidence.snippet: Mean-field models predict a large polarized EMC effect: a large modification of the spin-dependent g1 structure function for nuclei relative to their constituent nucleons, with implications for the Bjorken sum rule in medium.
status_evidence.claim: Some aspects of the in-medium polarized Bjorken sum rule have been investigated in mean-field models, indicating large nuclear modifications, but not yet linked to axial radiative corrections in mirror β decays.

status_evidence.title: The EMC Effect in Spin Structure Functions PR12-14-001
status_evidence.snippet: JLab proposal to measure the spin EMC effect in g1 of light nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental program to measure the spin-dependent EMC effect is still in progress, indicating the underlying nuclear modifications of g1,2 are not yet experimentally pinned down.
